report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to adopt an advice/guide-style, safety/compliance–oriented objective: it tends to produce cautious, normative recommendations (checklists, best practices), with legal/medical caveats and risk-mitigation framing, across general topics.

Reasoning from evidence:
- Imperative/advisory lead-ins at pos0 across many layers: top tokens like “Stay”, “Every”, “Consider”, “Do”, “Check”, “Non”, “optimize”, “ensure”, “adopt”, “adhere”, “proactive”, “mindful”, “recommend/recommendations” strongly indicate guidance/how‑to/checklist language rather than neutral narration.
- Consistent legal/medical/emergency nouns later in the sequence (pos2–pos4, layers ~19–25): “law/Law”, “wrong/incorrect”, “surgeon/clinic/surgery/treatment”, “rescue/volunteers”, “tragic/tragedy”. These are exactly the kinds of caveats and escalation-to-professional guidance that appear in safety/compliance copy (“comply with laws,” “seek medical attention,” “in emergencies…”).
- Broader safety/ethics/environmental register: tokens like “Sustainable”, “reduce”, “restoration”, “wildlife”, “relevant/normal/human” reinforce a risk‑aware, responsibility‑framed tone rather than, e.g., casual conversation or pure news.
- Structure/time/citation hints at careful, qualified exposition: pos1 repeatedly shows “Later/latter/ago/mention/visits/versions/Past,” consistent with hedged, context‑aware explanatory writing.
- Very large norm concentrated at pos0 across almost all layers suggests a strong, global style/prefix-like shift—typical of SFT that injects a “guidance/caution-first” persona affecting the whole continuation.

Together these point to a finetune that makes the model default to giving stepwise recommendations and safety/compliance caveats (medical/legal/emergency), i.e., a safety- and best‑practices advisor rather than a neutral web-text continuer.
